summary: Defines a Management Information Base module for Network Mobility support. It is used with network management protocols to monitor and control a Mobile IPv6 node that has NEMO functionality, such as a router that moves with its whole network.

plainLanguage.summary: A moving network, like the one on a train, needs a dashboard. This note defines the gauges and switches that let an administrator watch and control a mobile router.

questions: how to monitor mobile ipv6 nemo
how to monitor a nemo mobile router with snmp
subtitle: The SNMP management objects for watching and controlling Mobile IPv6 nodes that move whole networks.

tldr.problem: Operators had no standard way to monitor or control a node that implements Network Mobility (NEMO), such as a mobile router that carries its whole network from place to place.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC defines NEMO-MIB, an SMIv2 module with groups for common state, the mobile router, the home agent and notifications, plus tables for bindings, egress interfaces and mobile network prefixes.
tldr.outcome: A manager using SNMP can read binding, movement and error counters, switch NEMO on or off, and receive tunnel up and down notifications. Write access is sensitive, so SNMPv3 is recommended.

today: RFC 5488 is a Proposed Standard published in April 2009. The unit metadata shows no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: A MIB for Moving Networks
sections.content:
This memo defines a portion of the Management Information Base (MIB), the NEMO support MIB, for use with network management protocols. It is used to monitor and control a Mobile IPv6 node with NEMO functionality. MIB objects are generally accessed through the Simple Network Management Protocol (SNMP) and are defined with the Structure of Management Information. This module is compliant with SMIv2 (RFC 2578, RFC 2579 and RFC 2580), and the overall framework is described in RFC 3410.

The document is almost entirely the MIB module itself. It has no protocol messages of its own, only managed objects.
sections.plainLanguage: A MIB is a list of dials and counters that a router agrees to show to the person looking after it. This note is the list for routers that travel.

sections.title: Mobile IPv6 and NEMO Entities
sections.content:
Mobile IPv6 (RFC 3775) lets nodes remain reachable while moving around the IPv6 Internet. The NEMO Basic Support Protocol (RFC 3963) extends it so that an entire network can move. Goals and terminology are covered in RFC 4886 and RFC 4885.

Mobile routers typically implement NEMO, although a mobile router may also act as a mobile node. An entity that implements the NEMO protocol is called a NEMO entity, and this document defines managed objects to monitor and control such entities.

The module assumes implementations support the ifTable of the IF-MIB (RFC 2863). The MOBILEIPV6-MIB (RFC 4295) covers a mobile node, and implementations supporting both mobile node and NEMO functions SHOULD implement the objects from both MIBs. Address types come from the INET-ADDRESS-MIB (RFC 4001).
sections.plainLanguage: Imagine a bus that carries a whole classroom of computers. The bus has to tell the school where it is now so messages still find the class. This MIB lets an admin check how that is going.

sections.title: How the MIB Is Organized
sections.content:
The module is built from groups. nemoCore holds objects common to all NEMO entities. nemoMr models the mobile router service, including Dynamic Home Agent discovery and objects recording the router's movement. nemoHa models the home agent service, and nemoNotifications defines the asynchronous notifications. The module also defines a nemoCn group for the correspondent node and registers under mib-2 as number 184.

Five tables carry most of the detail: nemoBindingCacheTable models the Binding Cache on the home agent, nemoMrEgressIfTable lists configured egress interfaces, nemoMrBLTable models the Binding Update List on the mobile router, nemoHaCounterTable keeps registration statistics per mobile router, and nemoHaMobileNetworkPrefixTable lists the mobile network prefixes the home agent maintains.
sections.plainLanguage: The MIB is a filing cabinet with drawers: one for things every moving router shares, one for the router, one for its home base, and one for alarm bells.

sections.title: Tables of Bindings, Interfaces and Prefixes
sections.content:
The mobile router's nemoMrBLTable adds NEMO columns to a row of the MOBILEIPV6-MIB Binding Update List. Each row says whether the router registered in implicitMode (no Mobile Network Prefix Option in the Binding Update) or explicitMode (one or more such options), whether the Mobile Router Flag was set, the prefix lengths of the home and care-of addresses, the active egress interface index and the index of the tunnel to the home agent. nemoMrPrefixRegMode is the read-write object that selects the registration mode.

On the home agent, nemoBindingCacheTable extends Binding Cache entries with nemoBindingMrFlag and nemoBindingMrMode. nemoHaMobileNetworkPrefixTable is indexed by home address and a sequence number from 1 to 1024, and each row shows a prefix, its length and its source: configured by hand or learned from a bindingUpdate. The egress interface table gives each interface a priority between 0 and 255, a description and a roam hold-down time in seconds that avoids interface flapping.

Two limits are noted for implementers. If the home address in an index exceeds 112 octets (113 for the counter table), the object identifiers will have more than 128 sub-identifiers and cannot be accessed over SNMPv1, SNMPv2c or SNMPv3.
sections.plainLanguage: The tables are like logbooks. One lists how the router signed in with its home base, one lists the home base's guests, and one lists which doors, like Wi-Fi or cellular, the router can use.

sections.title: Counters and Notifications
sections.content:
The mobile router counts mobility messages sent and received, Modified Dynamic Home Agent Address Discovery requests and replies, and movements: back home, out of home, and from one foreign network to another. It also counts how often a better egress interface was found. Separate counters tally Binding Acknowledgements received with each NEMO-specific error, and the home agent keeps matching counters of Binding Updates it rejected.

The shared nemoCounterDiscontinuityTime holds the sysUpTime of the latest counter discontinuity, or zero if there has been none since the management subsystem was last re-initialized. Per-router counters on the home agent use their own nemoHaCtrDiscontinuityTime. The home agent also records when a Binding Cache entry was created and when a Binding Update was last accepted or rejected, as 11-byte DateAndTime values.

Two notifications are defined. nemoHomeTunnelEstablished and nemoHomeTunnelReleased are sent by the mobile router each time the tunnel between it and the home agent is set up or deleted, and carry the egress and tunnel interface indexes, the care-of address and the prefix lengths.
sections.plainLanguage: Counters are like a tally sheet of how many times the bus moved and how many times the school said no. The alarm bells ring when the bus connects to or drops its link to home.

sections.title: Compliance Statements
sections.content:
The module groups its objects into units such as nemoSystemGroup, nemoMrConfGroup, nemoHaStatsGroup and nemoNotificationGroup. Nine compliance statements say which groups an implementation must support. Every NEMO implementation needs the system group, which holds nemoCapabilities (mobile router and home agent support bits) and nemoStatus.

Variants cover Binding Cache monitoring, the mobile router, the home agent and notifications, and several have read-only forms where write access to objects such as nemoStatus is not required. The statements that involve addresses require support for global IPv6 addresses, with 16-octet address objects.
sections.plainLanguage: Compliance statements are checklists. They say which dials a router must show to count as supporting this MIB.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
Two read-write objects are called out. nemoStatus enables or disables NEMO and could be abused to disrupt communication that depends on it. nemoMrPrefixRegMode controls how mobile network prefixes are registered and could be abused to disrupt prefix setup. The home agent's mobile network prefix type, prefix and length objects reveal the configuration of the mobile router and may be sensitive or private, so even read access should be controlled.

Versions of SNMP before SNMPv3 did not include adequate security. The RFC RECOMMENDS the SNMPv3 security features with cryptographic authentication and privacy, and says deploying versions prior to SNMPv3 is NOT RECOMMENDED. Operators are responsible for giving access only to legitimate principals. IANA assigned the base arc 184 in the mib-2 tree for nemoMIB.
sections.plainLanguage: The switches on this dashboard could break the network if the wrong person flips them, so only trusted people should be allowed near, and the messages should be locked up with SNMPv3.
